reason: Section 13.1 covers several distinct Potable Water Advisory Committee topics: definition and composition, recommendation duties, internal procedure and consultations, and advisers or expense payments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Potable Water Advisory Committee definition, establishment, and membership
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 13.1(1) through 13.1(3) define the chief medical officer of health, establish the Committee, and specify its six-person composition and chairperson.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definition, establishment, membership composition, and chairperson rule for the Potable Water Advisory Committee.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Potable Water Advisory Committee recommendation duties
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 13.1(4) states the Committee's recommendation role on contaminant levels, significant health risk measures, owner notices, and other regulated matters.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what recommendations the Potable Water Advisory Committee must make about significant health risks, measures, notices, and regulated matters.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Committee quorum, procedure, sittings, and consultations
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 13.1(5) through 13.1(8) govern how the Committee sets quorum, makes procedure rules, sits as needed, and consults owners of water sources under consideration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Committee's quorum, procedure, sitting, and owner-consultation rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Committee advisers, remuneration, and expenses
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 13.1(9) through 13.1(11) authorize advisers and payments for certain members and persons appearing before the Committee.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may be engaged as Committee advisers and what remuneration or expenses may be paid.

reason: Section 14 is a large protected-area Designation Order provision with distinct topics for designation authority, order requirements and contents, publication, filing and registers, and compliance by affected persons.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Designation of protected watershed, aquifer, or recharge areas
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14(1) and 14(2) establish the authority to designate protected areas used as public water supply sources and require a commencement date.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Minister may designate protected watershed, aquifer, or ground water recharge areas and must provide a commencement date.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Protected-area requirements, schedules, and plans
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14(3) and 14(4) identify the requirements a Designation Order may impose and the schedule and protected-area description or plan it must include.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the requirements, schedule, and plan or description that may or must appear in a protected-area Designation Order.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Publication, filing, registration, notice, and registers for Designation Orders
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14(4.1) through 14(7) cover publication alternatives, pre-commencement filing and registry-office registration, newspaper notice, notice contents, and public inspection registers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the publication, filing, registration, notice, and register requirements for protected-area Designation Orders.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Compliance with protected-area Designation Order requirements
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14(8) and 14(9) distinguish compliance duties for persons already affected on commencement and persons who later acquire, propose, or commence affected activities, things, or uses.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when existing and later-affected persons must comply with protected-area requirements and how exemptions affect that duty.

reason: Section 14.1 covers several distinct Designation Order exemption topics: requesting and deciding exemptions, who and what an exemption covers, filing and legal treatment, compliance duties, and special rules for the order filed as New Brunswick Regulation 90-136.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Requesting and deciding protected-area exemptions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14.1(1) and 14.1(2) explain who may request an exemption, when and how the request is delivered, and the Minister's options to grant, acquire land, or refuse.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how affected persons request protected-area exemptions and what decisions the Minister may make on receipt.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Persons, land, and requirements covered by protected-area exemptions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14.1(3) and 14.1(4) specify the persons, successors, employees or agents, land parcel identifiers, requirements, and land description or plan that define the exemption's coverage.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a protected-area exemption must say about covered persons, successors, employees or agents, land identifiers, requirements, and land descriptions or plans.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Exemption legal treatment, filing, and compliance
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14.1(5) through 14.1(8) govern the exemption's Regulations Act treatment, exemption from subsection 14(5), optional registry filing, and compliance duty.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how protected-area exemptions are treated under the Regulations Act and section 14 filing rules, when they may be filed, and what compliance they require.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Exemptions for New Brunswick Regulation 90-136 requirements
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14.1(9) and 14.1(10) separately address exemption applications and modified application rules for requirements under the order filed as New Brunswick Regulation 90-136.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how exemptions from New Brunswick Regulation 90-136 requirements are requested and how subsections 14.1(2) to 14.1(8) apply with modifications.

reason: Section 14.11 is a cohesive delegation provision for exemption decisions, requiring written delegation, specifying how authority is exercised, and binding the delegate to the Minister's limits, terms, conditions, and requirements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Delegation of protected-area exemption decisions
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections work together on who may receive delegated exemption authority, written form, required delegation contents, and the delegate's duty to follow the delegation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Minister may delegate exemption grant or refusal authority and what limits and duties govern the delegate.

reason: Section 14.2 is a focused compensation and priority rule for land affected by Designation Orders or section 14 requirements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No injurious affection compensation for protected-area designation
proposedGroups.reason: The section states that designation, adjacency, and section 14 requirements do not by themselves injuriously affect land for compensation purposes, and gives the section priority over conflicting Act provisions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall why protected-area designation or related requirements do not by themselves create compensation and how section 14.2 prevails over conflicting Act provisions.

reason: Section 14.3 is a single registration duty for the Minister to register the order filed as New Brunswick Regulation 90-136 in the relevant Service New Brunswick registry office or offices.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration of New Brunswick Regulation 90-136 order

evidenceText: shall register, in accordance with paragraph 14(5)(b)
a copy of the order filed as New Brunswick Regulation 90-136
in the registry office of Service New Brunswick

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one registration duty tied to the counties where the protected areas related to the regulation are situated.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall where the Minister must register the order filed as New Brunswick Regulation 90-136.

reason: Section 14.4 is a single failure-or-refusal compliance order power for Designation Orders, exemption requirements, and the order filed as New Brunswick Regulation 90-136.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Orders to enforce Designation Orders and exemption requirements

evidenceText: if the Minister is satisfied, on reasonable and probable grounds
failing or refusing to comply, in whole or in part
may order the taking of such action as the Minister considers necessary

proposedGroups.reason: The provision identifies the standard for Ministerial satisfaction, the kinds of Designation Order and exemption non-compliance covered, and the action that may be ordered to effect compliance.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may order action to effect compliance with Designation Orders, exemption requirements, or the order filed as New Brunswick Regulation 90-136.

reason: Section 15 is a large watercourse and wetland alteration provision with distinct topics for planning and permits, owner maintenance and specification duties, Minister inspection and repair orders, non-compliant alteration orders, and public-interest removal when the owner cannot be ascertained.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Watercourse or wetland alteration planning, permits, terms, and exemptions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 15(1), 15(1.01), and 15(1.1) govern pre-project plan submission, permit requirements, permit terms and conditions, and regulatory exemptions or waivers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the planning, document, permit, permit-term, and exemption rules before undertaking watercourse or wetland alteration projects.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Owner duties to meet specifications and maintain structures
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 15(1.2) and 15(2) impose ongoing owner duties to meet original, permit, and approved specifications and maintain projects or structures in good repair.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the ongoing owner duties to meet specifications and keep watercourse or wetland projects and structures in good repair.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister inspection, information, repair, and compliance orders
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 15(3) authorizes Minister orders for inspection, documents and information, repairs or modifications, and compliance with permit terms or specifications.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the inspection, information, repair, modification, and specification-compliance orders available for watercourse or wetland projects or structures.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Orders for non-compliant watercourse or wetland alterations
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 15(4) separately addresses orders when an alteration or related work is not commenced, made, or carried out in compliance with the Act, regulations, permit terms, or Minister orders, directions, or demands.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what the Minister may order when a watercourse or wetland alteration is not compliant.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Public-interest removal when alteration or structure owner cannot be ascertained
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 15(5) is a separate removal power for public-interest removal of an alteration, structure, or thing from a watercourse or wetland when the owner cannot be ascertained.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may order public-interest removal from a watercourse or wetland at provincial expense because the owner cannot be ascertained.

reason: Section 16 is a single prohibition requiring the appropriate registration, licence, permit, or approval before engaging in specified well-drilling, well work, or incidental reconditioning or abandonment operations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Authorization required for well-drilling and related well work

evidenceText: engage in the business of well-drilling
undertake the boring, drilling, digging or redrilling of a well
unless that person is the holder of the appropriate registration, licence, permit or approval

proposedGroups.reason: The target identifies the regulated well-drilling and related activities and the required authorization condition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which well-drilling and related operations require the appropriate registration, licence, permit, or approval.

reason: Section 17 contains distinct inspector topics: Minister designation, broad inspection powers, private-dwelling entry limits, and detention of evidence.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Inspector designation and Clean Water Act inspection powers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 17(1) and 17(2) establish inspector designation and the inspection, testing, entry, and sampling powers used to administer the Act, including protected-area inspection powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how inspectors are designated and what entry, inspection, testing, and sampling powers they have under the Clean Water Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Private dwelling limits on Clean Water Act inspector entry
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 17(3) separately limits inspector entry into private dwellings to emergency, adult occupant consent, or Entry Warrants Act warrant situations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the emergency, consent, and entry-warrant bases that allow a Clean Water Act inspector to enter a private dwelling.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Inspector detention of evidence discovered under section 17
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 17(4) identifies what an inspector may detain, the evidentiary purpose, and the reasonable-grounds connection to a violation or failure to comply.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what Clean Water Act inspectors may detain as evidence after discovering it while acting under section 17.

reason: Section 18 is a focused duty for owners, persons in charge, employees, and agents to assist inspectors and furnish reasonably required information.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Assistance and information duties owed to Clean Water Act inspectors

evidenceText: shall give all reasonable assistance to an inspector
to enable the inspector to carry out the inspector’s duties
shall furnish the inspector with such information as the inspector may reasonably require

proposedGroups.reason: The provision contains one assistance-and-information obligation owed by specified persons connected to an area, land, place, or premises.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must assist Clean Water Act inspectors and provide information reasonably required for inspector duties.

reason: Section 19 is a single prohibition against obstructing or hindering inspectors in carrying out their duties under the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Prohibition on obstructing or hindering Clean Water Act inspectors

evidenceText: No person shall obstruct or hinder an inspector in the carrying out of the inspector’s duties under this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one inspector-protection prohibition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that no person may obstruct or hinder a Clean Water Act inspector carrying out duties under the Act.

reason: Section 20 is a single prohibition against knowingly making false or misleading oral or written statements to inspectors or other persons carrying out Act duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: False or misleading statements to Clean Water Act inspectors

evidenceText: No person shall knowingly make a false or misleading statement
to inspectors or other persons engaged in carrying out their duties

proposedGroups.reason: The provision contains one truthfulness obligation for statements made to inspectors or other duty-carrying persons under the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that knowingly false or misleading oral or written statements to Clean Water Act inspectors or other Act-duty persons are prohibited.

reason: Section 21 is a single designation authority allowing the Minister to designate analysts for the purposes of the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister designation of Clean Water Act analysts

evidenceText: The Minister may designate persons as analysts for the purposes of this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one operative authority identifying who may designate analysts and for what statutory purpose.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Minister may designate persons as analysts for the purposes of the Clean Water Act.

reason: Section 22 is a cohesive evidentiary provision for Minister statements and documents in prosecutions, including admissibility and proof, notice before production, and cross-examination with leave.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister documents and statements in Clean Water Act prosecutions
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections work together on how Minister documents, statements, and certified copies are used in prosecutions and what procedural protections apply to the opposing party.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how Minister documents and statements may be used in Clean Water Act prosecutions and what notice and cross-examination protections apply.
